title: verify: assert active generation and cover VPN/DNS/metrics
description:
`task deploy` computes the target toplevel at Taskfile.yml:40 but does not pass it to verify-host.sh (Taskfile.yml:54). verify-host.sh only checks that `/run/current-system/bin/switch-to-configuration` exists (scripts/verify-host.sh:50), so a stale or partially activated generation can pass. README claims the current system closure is checked.

The script also hardcodes incus/wireguard/unbound units and only checks incusbr0; it does not check incusbr-vpn, incus-runtime-config, DNS resolution, the VPN nftables masquerade, or the Incus metrics scrape. Cache reachability is warn-only (scripts/verify-host.sh:76-79), while README lists it with the failing checks.

Source: README.md:601-602, Taskfile.yml:40,54, scripts/verify-host.sh:50,62,70,76-79.
acceptance_criteria: Taskfile passes the expected `$system`; verify compares `readlink /run/current-system` and fails on mismatch; conditional checks cover incusbr-vpn, incus-runtime-config, DNS, and Incus metrics where enabled; cache behaviour is explicit in docs and code; the script is tested with a mock SSH target.

title: M1: prove the foundation (DR + host-loss + drift)
description: First milestone for the north star: one-command disaster recovery, survivability after losing either host, and nightly drift detection. These three prove the foundation for the self-operating fleet; close M1 when all three goals are done and one timed drill of each has passed.
acceptance_criteria: All three m1 goals are closed; a timed DR drill, a host power-loss drill, and a detected-and-fixed drift event have evidence.

title: GitOps with drift detection
description:
Every host change goes through git: PR -> nix flake check -> canary deploy -> verify -> rollout. Nightly verification detects failed units, wrong closures, DNS or firewall drift, and reports actionably. No manual SSH changes. Workload plan and drift stay in nix-workloads.

Related: homelab-7dg.7, homelab-7dg.10, nix-workloads-kvm, nix-workloads-4k8.
acceptance_criteria: Host changes are PR-gated; scheduled verification runs nightly and alerts on drift; a deliberately introduced drift is detected and fixed via the normal path.

title: Survive loss of either host
description:
Make critical services (DNS, identity, MQTT, Home Assistant) survive losing either rpi5-8gb or rpi5-4gb, or degrade explicitly. Decide replication/placement and whether a witness/quorum node is worth adding; handle the hardware-pinned Zigbee dongle as a planned outage. Success: pull one host's power; the house keeps working (lights/heating/MQTT) and monitoring tells the truth.

Related: homelab-7dg.5, homelab-7dg.9, nix-workloads-xp2, nix-workloads-sl8, nix-workloads-93o, nix-workloads-c6z.
acceptance_criteria: A documented failure model exists; critical services have a placement/replication decision; a timed power-loss drill on each host passes the agreed critical-path checks; accepted outages are explicit.

title: One-command disaster recovery
description:
From bare hardware (fresh SD/NVMe) plus this repo and the workload repo, rebuild both hosts and restore state with one command. Cover secrets/break-glass, bootstrap image, install, deploy, workload provision, and data restore. Target RTO under 1 hour and RPO under 24 hours, measured by a timed quarterly drill and automated restore verification. Start by automating the existing manual install/verify path; do not invent a new orchestrator.

Related: homelab-7dg.6, nix-workloads-m2x, nix-workloads-sl8, nix-workloads-5th, nix-workloads-3kb, nix-workloads-182.
acceptance_criteria: A documented single command or tiny wrapper takes a blank Pi to a verified host; a second command provisions and restores workloads; the drill is timed and passes; restore verification runs on a schedule.

title: North star: a self-healing two-node private cloud
description: Ambitious direction for the host layer: a two-node private cloud that rebuilds itself from git in under an hour, survives either Pi dying without waking the house, and needs no manual steps to stay healthy. The ten goals below are deliberately larger than the current beads; the first milestone is one-command DR, single-host-loss survivability, and nightly drift detection (label m1). Workload-side implementation and runbooks stay in nix-workloads; this epic owns host-layer slices and references the existing epics homelab-8ar and homelab-7dg. An explicit anti-goals decision records what we are not building.
acceptance_criteria: The north star is decomposed into tracked goals; M1 is defined and unblocked; anti-goals are recorded; host/workload boundaries are explicit.

title: devshell: include task, nixos-rebuild, zstd, and lint tools
description:
flake.nix includes opencode, beads, sops, cachix, ssh-to-age, wireguard-tools, and attic, but not `task`, `nixos-rebuild`, or `zstd`, even though AGENTS/README tell agents to run `task` and the Taskfile invokes `nixos-rebuild` and `zstd`. On this Mac those exist in ~/.nix-profile, not the devshell, so a fresh `nix develop` agent gets command-not-found. Consider adding shellcheck/nixfmt/fd for ad-hoc checks too.

Source: AGENTS.md:27-30, Taskfile.yml, flake.nix:95-114.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh `nix develop` can run `task --list`, `task fmt`, and the deploy/bootstrap toolchain without relying on a user profile; docs list any intentional host prerequisites.

title: agent: align .beads/README and config with JSONL workflow
description:
.beads/README.md tells agents to run `bd dolt push` and sync with Dolt, directly contradicting AGENTS.md (never run `bd dolt push`) and README (the tracked JSONL snapshot is the sync path). It also suggests `bd update --status done` instead of `bd close`.

.beads/config.yaml:53-58 says JSONL auto-export is disabled by default, while lines 76-78 enable `export.auto` with `git-add: true`.

Source: AGENTS.md:24-26, README.md:646-667, .beads/README.md:29-30,54, .beads/config.yaml:53-58,76-78.
acceptance_criteria: .beads/README.md has a repo-specific note or replacement pointing to AGENTS.md and the JSONL workflow; config comments match actual export.auto/git-add; no tracked doc recommends `bd dolt push`.
notes: Also observed while creating these issues: bd auto-export prints a repair hint recommending `bd dolt push`, which directly conflicts with the repo JSONL workflow. Consider suppressing or documenting that hint as part of this fix.

title: ci: build a host/image or document eval-only gate
description:
`checks.eval-all` only forces drvPath (flake.nix:160-166), and CI only runs `nix flake check` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:21,30); flake check also warns that `images` is unchecked. A config can evaluate and still fail to build, so deploys are currently the only build gate.

Add a cache-assisted build of `images.rpi5-bootstrap` and/or a host toplevel, or explicitly document that build failures are deploy-time only. Also consider shellchecking the Taskfile inline shell and linting the workflow.

Source: flake.nix:160-166, .github/workflows/ci.yml:21,30, Taskfile.yml.
acceptance_criteria: CI catches at least bootstrap image build failures with cache, or README/AGENTS explicitly state the eval-only gate; Taskfile inline shell is linted or extracted; the unchecked `images` warning is resolved or documented.

title: checks: add cross-file invariants and docs-path lint
acceptance_criteria: New checks fail on an orphaned host, missing inventory entry, broken CIDR, missing peer listenPort, silently skipped DNS zone, or stale local docs path; `nix flake check` remains quick.

title: docs: correct snapper cadence and stale module references
description:
README says snapper snapshots `/persist` on a nightly timeline, but `systemd.timers.snapper-timeline` evaluates to `OnCalendar=hourly`, and modules/storage.nix sets `TIMELINE_LIMIT_HOURLY = "8"`.

Also correct stale references: modules/site.nix:15 points at nonexistent `modules/incus/dns.nix`; modules/monitoring-agent.nix:7 says the metrics listener lives in preseed.nix instead of runtime.nix. The stale "not yet scripted" install bullet in README:687-689 is already tracked as homelab-8ar.1 and should not be duplicated.

Source: README.md:77, modules/storage.nix:82-88, modules/site.nix:15, modules/monitoring-agent.nix:7.
acceptance_criteria: README cadence matches the actual timer (or the timer is changed deliberately); both stale module references are corrected; docs point only to real files.

title: storage: persist journald explicitly
description:
README says `/var/log` plus persistent journald, but modules/storage.nix only persists `/var/log`. The generated journald.conf is `[Journal]\nAudit=keep` (no Storage), so systemd falls back to `auto`; `/var/log/journal` is not created by the repo, so local logs can stay volatile and disappear on reboot.

Use `services.journald.settings.Journal.Storage = "persistent"` (verified to emit `Storage=persistent`). Avoid the old `services.journald.storage` alias: in the pinned nixpkgs revision it currently throws a `Renaming error` because the target is a freeform option.

Source: README.md:74, modules/storage.nix:52-65.
acceptance_criteria: journald.conf contains Storage=persistent; /var/log/journal exists and survives a reboot; verify-host.sh checks it; README matches the config.

title: Parity audit: code, tests, docs, and agent surfaces
description: Repository-wide parity review (2026-10-24) found strong architectural alignment but drift between operational docs, deploy verification, test coverage, and agent-facing files. This epic groups the actionable follow-ups. Source: review of README.md, AGENTS.md, Taskfile.yml, flake.nix, modules/, scripts/, and .beads/.
acceptance_criteria: Every actionable parity finding has a child issue with evidence and acceptance criteria; after the children close, code, tests, docs, and agent-facing surfaces agree and no known drift remains untracked.

title: Decide anti-goals for the north star
description: Record what this project is deliberately not building, so ambition does not turn into accidental scope: no Kubernetes or bespoke control plane unless incus stops fitting; no chasing 99.99 percent (target 'the house works' and 'recovery is boring'); no third node only for HA unless it also buys a witness, offsite copy or test bed; no tuning matrix without a measured problem. Revisit only with evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The anti-goals are recorded as a decision and referenced from the north-star epic; future proposals that violate them are explicitly challenged.

title: Offline mode
description:
When the ISP, router, or cloud is down, the house keeps working: local DNS, NTP, auth, updates, and automation. Only genuinely remote things fail. Document the dependency graph and test by unplugging the uplink.

Related: homelab-7dg.2, homelab-7dg.9, nix-workloads-c6z, nix-workloads-env, nix-workloads-93o, nix-workloads-5u0.
acceptance_criteria: An uplink-down drill passes: local DNS, NTP, auth and automation still work; remote failures are explicit; the runbook lists what degrades.

title: Verifiable supply chain
description:
Treat the host as an appliance: reproducible closures, signed artifacts, SBOM, pinned inputs, retained caches, and a staged update bot with automatic rollback. A flake update should be boring: build, canary, verify, roll back on failure. Keep the vendor-kernel caveat explicit.

Related: homelab-8ar.3, homelab-8ar.9, homelab-7dg.10, nix-workloads-4k8, nix-workloads-6da.
acceptance_criteria: Host closures are reproducible or the exceptions are documented; artifacts are signed; an update bot opens PRs and gates on canary verification; cache retention covers rollback.

title: Zero static secrets
description:
Remove long-lived secrets from the operational path: short-lived certs, OIDC for humans, mTLS between workloads, automated step-ca issuance and rotation, hardware-backed break-glass keys. Keep only the root recovery material offline. Scope host-side pieces here; workload certs stay in nix-workloads.

Related: homelab-8ar.4, homelab-8ar.6, homelab-7dg.8, nix-workloads-182, nix-workloads-8xp, nix-workloads-s9w, nix-workloads-dkp.2.
acceptance_criteria: No long-lived shared credential is required for normal operation; certs rotate automatically; break-glass is documented and tested; the host trust bundle and Alloy mTLS are covered.

title: Self-operating fleet
description:
Build the detect -> file -> fix -> verify -> rollback loop: an agent spots drift or failure, files a bead, proposes a PR, tests in VMs, deploys to a canary host, runs verification, and rolls back on failure. Human approval remains the gate for risky changes. Reuse bd, nix flake check, scripts/verify-host.sh, and the deploy/rollback path; do not build a custom controller.

Related: homelab-8ar.2, homelab-7dg.7, nix-workloads-kvm, nix-workloads-a7q, nix-workloads-ka7.
acceptance_criteria: At least one class of drift or failure is fixed end-to-end by the loop with a human approval; the loop leaves an audit trail of bead, commit and verification; rollback is exercised.

title: The house never notices maintenance
description:
Routine reboots and upgrades should not interrupt the critical path. Move or duplicate services off the host being serviced, configure guest auto-start and ordering, sequence reboots, and keep monitoring and alerting meaningful during the window. Hardware-pinned workloads may take a planned outage. This is graceful maintenance, not full HA failover.

Related: homelab-7dg.5, nix-workloads-xp2, nix-workloads-4xa.
acceptance_criteria: A rehearsed maintenance runbook exists; a single-host reboot or upgrade preserves the agreed critical path; monitoring stays truthful; timing and accepted outages are recorded.

title: Make guest DNS survive loss of the default host
description:
Guests on rpi5-4gb resolve through rpi5-8gb at 10.6.0.3. If the default host dies, name resolution (and TLS/MQTT/backup reconnects) fails. Host-side scope: make both host resolvers independently usable/redundant and document the interface; guest wiring stays in nix-workloads.

Source: nix-workloads-93o.
acceptance_criteria: Either host can serve the required zones/records alone; the guest resolver policy is documented and tested with the default resolver unavailable.

title: Baseline host hardening and access lifecycle
description:
Add a host baseline for SSH/user/sudo policy, the no-AppArmor trade-off, WireGuard peer add/remove/rotation, Incus client certificates, and credentials outside sops (Attic/Cachix/router/GitHub/SSH). Include a join/leave procedure and a cheap drift check. The guest/identity side stays in nix-workloads.

Source: nix-workloads-rgc.
acceptance_criteria: Host baseline is documented and enforced where possible; peer/client-cert lifecycle is repeatable; drift is detectable.

title: Define the host/workload contract and rehearse a bare-metal rebuild
description:
nix-workloads assumes host-provided building blocks: incusbr-vpn, host Unbound, CA/cache trust, client certs, the persistent pool and platform CA. Write the contract down (required host settings/versions and consumed interfaces), add a cheap compatibility check, and rehearse a rebuild from this repo through install, plan/deploy and verify.

Source: nix-workloads-mi1 and nix-workloads-m2x.
acceptance_criteria: The contract is documented and checked; a fresh host install plus workload provision/restore is rehearsed and timed.

title: Make host maintenance and reboots safe
description:
A host reboot or upgrade can take internet/DNS, identity, MQTT/Zigbee and lights/heating with it. Define what must stay up and where, implement a single-host maintenance path (move/duplicate critical services, guest auto-start, reboot sequencing, monitoring during the window), and rehearse it. Hardware-pinned workloads (Zigbee dongle) may accept a planned outage.

Source: nix-workloads-xp2.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, rehearsed maintenance runbook exists; guest auto-start and ordering are configured; a single-host reboot preserves the agreed critical path.

title: Schedule btrfs scrub and SMART self-tests
description:
The host pools are btrfs with no scheduled scrub or SMART self-tests. Add systemd timers for scrub and short/long SMART tests on both hosts, alert on failures and pending sectors, and write a failing-device runbook (no RAID: scrub detects, backups restore).

Source: nix-workloads-cme.
acceptance_criteria: Timers fire on both hosts; failures/pending sectors are exported and alerted; the runbook covers replace/restore.

title: Own host time synchronization
description:
TLS, ACME, logs and incident timelines depend on correct time, but this repo does not pin an NTP source, fallback, or drift alerting for the hosts. Decide chrony vs timesyncd and internal vs public sources; apply it to both hosts (and note the guest policy), and monitor offset.

Source: nix-workloads-5u0.
acceptance_criteria: Both hosts have a documented NTP configuration with a fallback; offset/drift is monitored; the behavior when the internet is down is documented.

title: Restore host memory/zram defaults
description:
Experiment-era zram/swappiness/page-cluster/PSI tuning is still applied to both hosts. Prefer upstream/NixOS defaults for the mostly-idle 8GB/4GB pair: remove KSM and density knobs, keep PSI only if still useful, document any remaining non-default and the rollback. Re-run the E4 zram decision only after the E1/E2 cache rebalance settles.

Source: nix-workloads-94k.3 and nix-workloads-e10.
acceptance_criteria: modules/zram.nix and host memory settings contain only documented, justified non-defaults; a deploy and verify pass; EXPERIMENTS.md references are updated or retired.

title: Host-layer follow-ups from nix-workloads
description: Scanned nix-workloads' beads export (67 issues: 58 open, 2 in progress, 2 deferred, 5 closed) for work that requires changes in the host layer. The 11 children below are host-owned slices; the workload-side implementation and runbooks remain tracked in nix-workloads with the source IDs in each description. Existing host issues already cover parts of sops recipients (.4), Incus exposure (.5), root-CA rotation (.6), VM tests (.2), and Zigbee docs (.10); those were cross-referenced rather than duplicated.
acceptance_criteria: Each host-owned slice is tracked with its nix-workloads source; duplicated workload work stays in nix-workloads; cross-references are recorded on overlapping host issues.

title: Cache vendor linux-rpi builds
description:
Vendor-kernel builds have no public Hydra jobset, so a `nix flake update` that bumps nixos-hardware can trigger a multi-hour build before a deploy. `task cache-push` pushes only an already-built host closure. Add a path that builds and pushes new kernel closures promptly (scheduled CI job or a documented pre-update cache step) to Cachix/Attic.

Source: README 'Known risks' (vendor kernel builds are uncached).
acceptance_criteria: A flake-input bump has a documented, low-effort way to populate the new kernel closure in Cachix/Attic; the README risk is updated or removed.

title: Check that every host key is a sops recipient
description:
A host whose SSH host key is missing from `.sops.yaml` silently fails secret decryption at boot, so incus gets no ACME credentials and no certificate is issued. Add a check (flake check or `scripts/verify-host.sh`) that every host in `inventory.nix`/`hosts/` has a matching age recipient in `.sops.yaml` and that the encrypted files decrypt with it.

Source: README 'Known risks' (sops).
acceptance_criteria: A missing recipient fails a local or CI check with a clear error before deploy; adding a host documents the rekey step.
notes: Cross-repo: host slice of nix-workloads-182 (break-glass/offline recipient + consumer check); workload secrets stay there.

title: Backlog migrated from README scan
description: Repository-wide scan (README.md, AGENTS.md, Taskfile.yml, modules/, scripts/, .github/) found no TODO/FIXME comments and no open GitHub issues; the actionable work lives in README's 'Known risks' and 'Future paths'. This epic groups that backlog. Non-actionable risks (PSU/cooling, ACME availability and rate limits, disko legacy-table warning, impermanence review process) stay as documentation and are not tracked as tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Every actionable README item has a focused child issue with its source and acceptance criteria; README no longer duplicates tracker state.

title: docs: clarify host scope and site vs local.site
description:
AGENTS.md says `hosts/*.nix` tune only local.incus/local.wireguard/local.dns plus hostName/stateVersion, but `hosts/rpi5-bootstrap.nix` legitimately sets sdImage.*, services.getty, environment.systemPackages, boot.supportedFilesystems, site.permitRootLogin, and system.nixos.variant_id.

There are also two namespaces: modules/ssh-access.nix defines `site.*` (SSH policy shared with bootstrap), while modules/site.nix defines `local.site.*` (main-host infrastructure). AGENTS only documents `local.site`, which can mislead an agent.

Source: AGENTS.md:15-17, hosts/rpi5-bootstrap.nix, modules/ssh-access.nix:3, modules/site.nix:9.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md says "permanent hosts" and documents the bootstrap exception; `site` versus `local.site` is explained (or renamed) so an agent knows where to change SSH policy versus shared site infrastructure.

title: docs: document cgroup, NVMe, and zram collectors
description:
modules/cgroup-metrics.nix, modules/nvme-wear.nix, and modules/zram.nix publish node_exporter textfile metrics (`node_cgroup_memory_*`, `node_nvme_*`, `node_zram_*`), and zram swap is enabled, but the README Monitoring section never mentions them. Add a short paragraph so the host monitoring surface is discoverable.

Source: README.md:411-437, modules/cgroup-metrics.nix, modules/nvme-wear.nix, modules/zram.nix.
acceptance_criteria: README Monitoring section lists the three collectors, their metric families, collection intervals, and zram swap; no code change required.

title: A 10-year homelab
description:
Make the project maintainable for a decade: spare hardware, hardware lifecycle and replacement plan, upgrade cadence, decision ledger, runbooks, and no single point of human failure. Any competent agent or human should be able to operate it from the repo.

Related: homelab-7dg.6, homelab-7dg.10, homelab-8ar.1, homelab-8ar.8, nix-workloads-4k8, nix-workloads-s3r, nix-workloads-rp6, nix-workloads-182.
acceptance_criteria: Hardware lifecycle, spares and upgrade cadence are documented; every critical runbook exists; a new operator or agent can install, deploy, verify and recover from the docs alone.

title: Energy, thermal and wear-aware placement
description:
Measure power, throttling, SoC/NVMe/SD wear, and capacity; use that to place workloads, avoid heat and write amplification, and replace hardware before failure. Forecast days-to-full and wear. Delete tuning that is not justified by measurements.

Related: homelab-7dg.1, homelab-7dg.3, homelab-7dg.4, nix-workloads-ozj, nix-workloads-cme, nix-workloads-13n, nix-workloads-94k.
acceptance_criteria: Power, thermal, wear and capacity metrics exist with forecasts and alerts; placement decisions use them; a seasonal review records headroom; experiment-era tuning is removed or justified.

title: TLS/mTLS for the host metrics path
description:
Host Alloy remote_write to the monitoring workload should use TLS+mTLS with the platform CA. Update modules/monitoring-agent.nix and certificate provisioning; the monitoring server and workload-side Alloy stay in nix-workloads.

Source: nix-workloads-dkp.4.
acceptance_criteria: Host Alloy verifies the monitoring endpoint and presents a client cert; no skip_verify; metrics keep flowing after the switch.

title: Define the host nixpkgs upgrade cadence
description:
flake.lock is updated by hand; define a host cadence for nixpkgs updates and deploys (dev/homelab, snapshots, rollback, verification). The workload base-image cadence and the 12 image strings stay in nix-workloads.

Source: nix-workloads-4k8.
acceptance_criteria: A documented host update cadence exists and has been exercised once end to end.

title: Schedule host verification and drift detection
description:
task verify and nix flake check only run by hand, so a failed unit, wrong closure, DNS record or firewall drift stays invisible. Add a scheduled host-side verification (systemd timer or CI) with actionable alerts; workload plan/drift stays in nix-workloads.

Source: nix-workloads-kvm.
acceptance_criteria: Host verification runs on a schedule and alerts on failure; the runbook says what to do when it fires.

title: Add host thermal, throttle and wear collectors
description:
Both Pis sit in a ~28C closet. Audit host-side coverage for SoC temperature, throttle/undervoltage flags, NVMe/SD wear and lifetime writes, and fan/thermal state; add missing collectors and export them for the workload dashboards. Alert thresholds and panels stay in nix-workloads.

Source: nix-workloads-ozj.
acceptance_criteria: Missing host metrics are collected and visible; thresholds/panels are linked from the workload issue; seasonal headroom is documented.

title: Document and check root CA rotation
description:
Internal TLS trust is pinned to the vendored Esselius root CA. Rotating step-ca without updating `certs/esselius-root-ca.crt` breaks Attic substitution and logs TLS warnings on every Nix invocation. Add a rotation runbook and a check that the vendored root still validates the Attic endpoint.

Source: README 'Known risks' (internal TLS trust).
acceptance_criteria: A documented rotation procedure exists and scripts/verify-host.sh or CI detects a stale or mismatched root.
notes: Cross-repo: host trust-bundle slice of nix-workloads-s9w and nix-workloads-8xp; CA root custody/rotation stays there.

title: Decide and narrow Incus API/UI exposure
description:
Incus listens on `core.https_address = ":8443"` and the firewall opens the port globally, so the API/UI is reachable from the LAN and the VPN, not just `wg0`. Client auth is certificate-based. Decide whether the broader exposure is wanted; if not, narrow the listener and nftables rule to the LAN/VPN addresses or `wg0`.

Source: README 'Known risks' (Incus API/UI listens on all interfaces).
acceptance_criteria: The intended exposure is documented; if narrowed, port 8443 is no longer reachable from untrusted networks and scripts/verify-host.sh still passes.
notes: Cross-repo: host listener/firewall slice of nix-workloads-485 and nix-workloads-rgc; the workload exposure matrix stays there.

title: CI: add NixOS VM tests
description:
The CI comment reserves `checks.aarch64-linux` for 'future NixOS VM tests'. No VM tests exist today. Add at least one VM test that boots a host config and asserts core units (incus, unbound, wg) or at least evaluates/boots the bootstrap image, wired through `mkChecks` so the macOS and aarch64-linux check sets stay in sync.

Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml and flake.nix `mkChecks`.
acceptance_criteria: A NixOS VM test runs under  on aarch64-linux; the macOS check set evaluates the same attributes; CI stays green.
notes: Cross-repo: guest VM tests are nix-workloads-udk; this issue covers host/bootstrap VM coverage.

title: README: drop stale 'not yet scripted' install bullet
description:
README 'Verification status' still says the mount + `nixos-enter` dance was 'exercised by hand several times, not yet scripted', while a later bullet states `nixos-anywhere --disko-mode mount` now automates it and the manual chroot is no longer required. Remove or rewrite the stale bullet so the status list matches the current soft-reset path.

Source: README 'Verification status'.
acceptance_criteria: README no longer claims the manual SD population is unscripted; the soft-reset bullet is the single description of how the SD boot partition is populated.

title: Document Zigbee passthrough and multi-host scaling
description:
README lists Zigbee passthrough details and secondary hosts at scale as additive future work; both Pis already have WireGuard, DNS, and cross-host routing. Write the concrete steps (USB device passthrough, per-host addressing, inventory/site changes) and validate one Zigbee device on an instance.

Source: README 'Future paths'.
acceptance_criteria: A playbook documents Zigbee passthrough and adding a third host; the steps are verified against the current modules.
notes: Cross-repo: device-level Zigbee failure/OTA/RF work stays in nix-workloads-629, nix-workloads-xkz, and nix-workloads-3iq.

title: Re-evaluate mainline kernel for Pi 5
description:
Vendor `linux-rpi` is used because mainline produced `rp1_driver -22` against the firmware DTBs. Re-test mainline once nixos-hardware/nixpkgs settle the Pi 5 DTB story (tracked via NixOS/nixos-hardware#78): USB/Ethernet, NVMe, and an incus VM guest on 16K pages.

Source: README kernel decision and 'Future paths'.
acceptance_criteria: A documented test result either keeps the vendor kernel with an updated rationale or moves the hosts to mainline with verification evidence.

title: Add IPv6 to the incusbr-vpn bridge
description:
`incusbr-vpn` is deliberately IPv4-only (`ipv6.address = "none"` and the masquerade table is family `ip`); IPv6 is out of scope until added deliberately. Add IPv6 addressing/NAT on both hosts, or record the permanent out-of-scope decision.

Source: README 'VPN-reachable instances'.
acceptance_criteria: Either IPv6 is configured and verified across both hosts, or the README states the permanent decision and this issue is closed.

title: NVMe-only boot once U-Boot 2026.10 lands in nixpkgs
description:
Boot files currently live on microSD because nixpkgs' U-Boot cannot read them from NVMe. Upstream NVMe boot landed for U-Boot 2026.10. Once nixpkgs ships it, add an NVMe FAT partition to disko, set EEPROM `BOOT_ORDER` to include NVMe, and retire the SD from daily duty. Fold in the M.2 hat EEPROM quirks (nvmd/nixos-raspberrypi #117).

Source: README 'Future paths' and the boot-device decision.
acceptance_criteria: Host boots entirely from NVMe with the SD removed; install/rebuild/rollback playbooks are updated; SD remains only as optional recovery.
